queries: WITH j AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), d AS (SELECT ID, SEX, igm, igm - (SELECT AVG(igm) FROM j) AS dev FROM j), x AS (SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.igm, d.dev, d.dev - (SELECT AVG(d2.dev) FROM d d2 WHERE d2.SEX = d.SEX) AS excess FROM d) SELECT ID, SEX, igm AS `aCL IgM`, dev AS deviation, excess AS excess_over_sex_avg FROM x WHERE excess > 0 ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10

WITH j AS (SELECT e.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), d AS (SELECT ID, SEX, igm, igm - (SELECT AVG(igm) FROM j) AS dev FROM j), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(dev) AS avg_dev FROM d GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID AS ID, d.SEX AS SEX, d.igm AS `aCL IgM`, d.dev AS deviation_from_overall_mean, d.dev - s.avg_dev AS excess_over_sex_avg_deviation FROM d JOIN s ON d.SEX = s.SEX WHERE d.dev > s.avg_dev ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg_deviation DESC, d.ID LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each entry is one examination row (a patient with several examinations can appear several times); the overall mean of aCL IgM is taken over examinations that match a patient, ignoring NULLs.
Rows with NULL aCL IgM have a NULL deviation and are excluded. Patients with NULL SEX match no group, so their sex average is NULL and they are excluded; blank-string SEX forms its own group.
Ties in the excess are broken arbitrarily, since the request gives no tiebreaker.

responses.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT e.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), d AS (SELECT ID, SEX, igm, igm - (SELECT AVG(igm) FROM j) AS dev FROM j), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(dev) AS avg_dev FROM d GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID AS ID, d.SEX AS SEX, d.igm AS `aCL IgM`, d.dev AS deviation_from_overall_mean, d.dev - s.avg_dev AS excess_over_sex_avg_deviation FROM d JOIN s ON d.SEX = s.SEX WHERE d.dev > s.avg_dev ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg_deviation DESC, d.ID LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each examination row is one entry, so a patient ID can appear more than once. The overall mean is taken over examination rows that match a patient and have a non-null aCL IgM.

Rows with a NULL SEX are excluded, because the join on SEX = SEX matches nothing for NULL. A blank-string SEX is its own group. NULL aCL IgM rows have NULL deviation, so they are excluded by the > filter.
Ties are broken by ID ascending. The request does not specify a tie-break.

responses.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT e.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), d AS (SELECT ID, SEX, igm, igm - (SELECT AVG(igm) FROM j) AS dev FROM j), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(dev) AS avg_dev FROM d GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.igm AS `aCL IgM`, d.dev AS deviation_from_overall_mean, d.dev - s.avg_dev AS excess_over_sex_avg_deviation FROM d JOIN s ON s.SEX = d.SEX WHERE d.dev > s.avg_dev ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg_deviation DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The overall mean of aCL IgM is computed only over examinations that match a patient (after the inner join), ignoring NULL values.
Each output row is one examination (a patient with several examinations can appear more than once). The result keeps the patient ID, SEX and that examination's aCL IgM.
Rows with NULL SEX or NULL aCL IgM are excluded from the output, because they cannot be compared against a sex average or a mean. Ties in the ranking are broken arbitrarily.
